common.whyIntro: Women and girls in Kakuma Refugee Camp face many challenges, including financial hardship, interrupted education, limited access to skills training, and barriers to employment and healthcare. For teenage mothers, these challenges can be even greater as they balance childcare with their education and personal development. At Women Without Borders Hub, we believe every girl and young woman deserves the opportunity to overcome these barriers, discover her potential, and build a better future. By promoting education, practical skills, mentorship, health awareness, and economic empowerment, we aim to create opportunities for women and girls to grow in confidence, strengthen their independence, and contribute to their communities.

quoteSection.quote2: I founded Women Without Borders Hub because I believe that every girl and young woman deserves a chance to create a better future, regardless of the challenges she faces. Too many talented young women have dreams that remain out of reach because of financial hardship, limited opportunities, and barriers that hold them back. I want to help change that by creating opportunities for learning, empowerment, and personal growth, where every girl can discover her strengths, find her voice, and move forward with confidence.

secondChanceDetail.intro: We support girls and women in Kakuma Refugee Camp, Kenya, who wish to continue their education, overcome barriers to learning, and build a better future. We believe that education is a right and that every girl and woman deserves the opportunity to learn, grow, and reach her full potential.
secondChanceDetail.whatImageAlt: A woman studying during a learning session
whatParagraphs: Our Second Chance Education programme focuses on supporting girls and women whose education has been interrupted or who have not had the opportunity to complete their studies. We recognize that financial difficulties, family responsibilities, displacement, and other life challenges can make it difficult to continue learning. Through this programme, we promote the importance of returning to education and encourage girls and women to pursue their learning goals with confidence and determination.

We believe that access to education can help women and girls gain knowledge, strengthen their independence, participate more actively in their communities, and create better opportunities for themselves and their families.

srhrDetail.title: Promoting Knowledge, Dignity, and Informed Choices
intro: At Women Without Borders Hub, we believe that every girl and young woman deserves access to reliable information about her sexual and reproductive health in a safe, respectful, and supportive environment.

In Kakuma Refugee Camp, stigma, cultural barriers, limited awareness, and difficulty accessing accurate health information can make it hard for some young people to discuss sexual and reproductive health openly. Our SRHR programme promotes age-appropriate education, peer learning, and community awareness to help address these challenges.
srhrDetail.howIntro: We create opportunities for girls and young women to learn, ask questions, share knowledge, and build confidence to make informed decisions about their health and well-being.

whatWeDo.title: What We Do
intro: Livelihood & Economic Empowerment is one of our core programme areas. We work alongside women and girls, community members, educators, local organizations, and potential partners to identify barriers and explore practical ways to expand access to economic opportunities.

Our programme focuses on building knowledge, confidence, practical abilities, and connections that can help participants take steps toward employment, entrepreneurship, and sustainable income generation.

areas.title: Entrepreneurship and Small Business Development
areas.imageAlt: Women taking part in the Entrepreneurship and Small Business Development activity in Kakuma
paragraphs: We promote entrepreneurship as one possible pathway toward economic independence. Through business learning and mentorship opportunities, women and girls can explore how to identify business ideas, understand customer needs, plan their activities, and develop the knowledge needed to manage a small business.

Topics may include identifying business opportunities, basic business planning, budgeting, record-keeping, customer service, pricing, marketing, and managing income and expenses. These skills can help aspiring entrepreneurs make informed decisions and approach business activities with greater confidence.

We also recognize the importance of learning from people with practical business experience. Where opportunities are available, connecting participants with local entrepreneurs and business mentors can help them understand common challenges and learn from real-life experiences.

areas.title: Skills Development and Vocational Training
areas.imageAlt: Women taking part in the Skills Development and Vocational Training activity in Kakuma
paragraphs: Practical skills can open doors to employment, self-employment, and other livelihood opportunities. We aim to encourage access to relevant skills development and vocational learning that responds to the interests of participants and the needs of the local community.

Depending on available training opportunities and partnerships, this may include practical, technical, creative, or service-related skills that can help participants prepare for work or explore small income-generating activities.

Our approach emphasizes the value of continuous learning, practical experience, and the confidence to apply newly acquired skills. We seek to support pathways through which women and girls can identify their strengths and make informed decisions about their future.

areas.title: Business Mentorship and Guidance
areas.imageAlt: Women taking part in the Business Mentorship and Guidance activity in Kakuma
paragraphs: Starting a business or pursuing employment can be challenging, especially for people who have limited access to professional networks and experienced advisers. Mentorship can help participants explore their goals, understand potential challenges, and identify realistic next steps.

Through mentorship opportunities, women and girls may receive guidance on setting goals, developing business ideas, improving decision-making, building confidence, and identifying resources that could support their progress.

We value mentorship that respects each participant's circumstances and encourages them to recognize their abilities. By learning from others and sharing experiences, participants can develop a stronger understanding of the opportunities available to them.

areas.title: Apprenticeships and Work Experience
areas.imageAlt: Women taking part in the Apprenticeships and Work Experience activity in Kakuma
paragraphs: Practical work experience can help bridge the gap between learning and employment. Where suitable opportunities are available, we seek to encourage connections with skilled professionals, businesses, training providers, and other community partners that may offer apprenticeships or supervised learning experiences.

These opportunities can help participants gain practical knowledge, understand workplace expectations, develop professional habits, and become more familiar with the skills required in different fields.
Work-based learning can also help participants identify their interests, strengthen their confidence, and explore possible pathways toward employment or self-employment.

areas.title: Market Linkages and Networking
areas.imageAlt: Women taking part in the Market Linkages and Networking activity in Kakuma
paragraphs: Access to customers, suppliers, professional contacts, and reliable information can make a difference for people who want to develop their livelihoods. We recognize that having a skill or business idea is only one part of the journey; participants may also need connections that help them find customers and explore markets.

Through potential partnerships and community networks, we aim to encourage opportunities for women and girls to learn about market needs, connect with relevant service providers, share ideas, and identify possible routes for promoting their products or services.
Stronger networks can help participants exchange knowledge, learn from other entrepreneurs, and explore opportunities to grow their activities over time.

areas.title: Employment Readiness and Referrals
areas.imageAlt: Women taking part in the Employment Readiness and Referrals activity in Kakuma
paragraphs: For women and girls who want to pursue employment, preparing for work can involve more than technical skills. Communication, teamwork, problem-solving, time management, and confidence can all be important when seeking and maintaining employment.

We aim to promote awareness of employment preparation and, where appropriate opportunities exist, connect participants with relevant training providers, employers, job information, or employment referral services.

This support may include guidance on preparing for job opportunities, understanding workplace expectations, identifying relevant skills, and exploring available career pathways. Referrals depend on the availability and suitability of opportunities and do not guarantee employment.

areas.title: Financial Awareness and Responsible Money Management
areas.imageAlt: Women taking part in the Financial Awareness and Responsible Money Management activity in Kakuma
paragraphs: Understanding how to manage money can help individuals make informed decisions about their personal finances and livelihood activities. We encourage the development of basic financial awareness, including planning expenses, saving where possible, managing business income, keeping financial records, and understanding the difference between costs, revenue, and profit.
These skills can support participants as they plan for their needs, evaluate business ideas, and work toward their financial goals.

We also recognize that financial circumstances differ from person to person. Our approach aims to promote practical, realistic learning that respects participants' situations and supports informed decision-making.

areas.title: Confidence, Leadership, and Economic Participation
areas.imageAlt: Women taking part in the Confidence, Leadership, and Economic Participation activity in Kakuma
paragraphs: Economic empowerment involves more than earning an income. It also includes having the confidence to make decisions, express ideas, participate in community life, and pursue personal goals.
We encourage women and girls to recognize their strengths, develop their leadership abilities, and take an active role in decisions that affect their livelihoods and futures.
By promoting confidence, collaboration, and access to information, we aim to support participants in becoming more active contributors to their households and communities.

ourApproach.title: Our Approach
ourApproach.intro: We aim to develop livelihood initiatives that are practical, inclusive, community-informed, and responsive to the experiences of the people we serve.

items.title: Community-led design
items.text: We value the experiences, priorities, and ideas of women and girls. Listening to community members helps identify relevant needs and shape activities that are better suited to their circumstances.

items.title: Safe and inclusive participation
items.text: We aim to promote respectful learning environments where participants are treated with dignity, have opportunities to contribute, and can participate without discrimination. Safeguarding and appropriate support should remain central to programme activities.

items.title: Practical and relevant learning
items.text: We recognize the importance of skills that participants can apply in everyday life, business activities, training, or employment pathways. Activities should respond to participants' interests and available opportunities.

items.title: Mentorship and collaboration
items.text: We value cooperation with community groups, local businesses, training providers, employers, educators, and other organizations that can contribute knowledge, resources, or relevant opportunities.

items.title: Access to opportunities
items.text: Where possible, we aim to connect participants with information about training, business development, markets, apprenticeships, and employment pathways.

items.title: Learning and accountability
items.text: We seek to learn from programme activities, listen to participant feedback, and communicate progress transparently. Where activities are implemented, monitoring can help us understand participation, identify challenges, and improve future support.
